answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independently verified tasks reveal fraud. Because reputation and access accrue to the bonded identity, an attacker cannot cheaply mint a meadow of disposable accounts: every Sybil must tie up capital, and detected deception destroys it. The bond should scale with the privilege claimed, not pretend to prove a person’s uniqueness; shale-backed collateral or nectar rewards do not change that core cost.
